newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soybean plantings leap ahead by Nov 7.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soybean plantings leap ahead by Nov 7.

text.p: Brazilian soybean plantings were 29 percent completed by Nov 7 against 18 percent by Nov 9, 1995, and an average of the past five years of 21 percent, consultant Safras e Mercado said.
Plantings in the week to Nov 7 showed a dramatic improvement given that only 10 percent of the crop had been sowed by Oct 31, according to Safras.
The quicker pace Safras attributed to a desire to take advantage of good soil moisture following recent rains plus also the higher chances of a second winter corn harvest.

Problems selling wheat as well as good soybean prices have meant farmers are preferring to plant soybeans, either reducing or only maintaining area planted to the main corn crop while planning to sow a larger area to corn in the winter.
The high percentage of area planted by Nov 7 has only been surpassed in 1993 when 38 percent of plantings had been completed by this stage, Safras said.
